conclusion: No blocking implementation defect found in the reviewed unique-edge build path. The mesh is derived from quantized source-member unions before tile clipping; real sampled tile edges are deduplicated and matching at the sampled seams.
constructionOrder: Validate original GPKG hash and 1500 source dates
Project original locality geometry onto the same global MVT grid for each zoom
Filter TYPE 8 and any XX membership; union by complete literal ADM1 strings
Take boundaries of globally uncut group polygons, including interior rings
Union linework on grid_size=1 and line-merge to remove coincident segments
Intersect the line network with each buffered tile rectangle; deduplicate snap-coincident clipped lines again
Encode and decode MVT and compare its line set to clipped input
tileFrameFinding: No polygon boundary is taken after tile clipping. The helper synthetic crossing test gives 20 units of genuine linework instead of the 40 units from clip-then-boundary. The 1-grid line coincident with one sampled buffer frame exists inside the neighboring tile, confirming its source continuity.

quantizationLimitations.coordinateRoundingNote: One initial axis-rounding step is <=0.5 cell per axis, but this is not an end-to-end Hausdorff bound: valid_output can remove collapsed holes/parts; union noding and clipping also snap.
quantizationLimitations.renderScale: One grid cell is 1/16 CSS px at a tile native zoom with 512px tiles. Overzoom amplifies this; at map z15 with z10 source it is 2px.
quantizationLimitations.seamNote: Common global input grid avoids independently shifted data origins, but integer-grid clipping can slightly change diagonal slopes between adjacent buffers. Exact seam equality is not guaranteed; inspect sample magnitudes.

scope: Independent code reading, four small actual-helper experiments, four z8 tile samples and three adjacent seams; no duplicate full build or full-tile audit was run by this reviewer. The earlier verifier layer-schema omission has been corrected by the build agent.
